key_terms.meaning: One rectangular element on screen that draws itself and can receive touch; the base class of every widget such as Button or TextView.
A View that holds child Views and positions them; every layout class extends ViewGroup.
An XML file under res/layout that declares a view tree; inflated into objects at runtime by setContentView.
Layout that stacks children in one row or column, using android:orientation and android:layout_weight.
Layout that positions each child by constraints to parent or sibling edges; the default for new screens in Android Studio.
Size constants: match_parent fills the parent's space, wrap_content takes only as much as the content needs.
dp = density-independent pixel for sizes (1 dp = 1/160 inch); sp = scale-independent pixel for text, also scaled by the user's font-size setting.
Any change such as rotation, keyboard, language or screen size that Android reports to the app by restarting the activity.
Callback where the activity puts small UI state into a Bundle before it is destroyed.
Manifest attribute that tells Android not to recreate the activity for listed changes; you then handle onConfigurationChanged yourself.
A strip at the top owned by the activity, showing the title, action buttons and the overflow list.
The menu built in onCreateOptionsMenu() from a menu XML file, shown as action icons plus overflow items.
Object implementing Adapter that converts a data item into a row View on demand; examples are ArrayAdapter and RecyclerView.Adapter.
Scrolling view that asks an adapter for row views as rows scroll into sight, so it never stores the data.
DatePicker, TimePicker and NumberPicker widgets, each with its own get/set methods and change listener.
ImageView attribute (centerCrop, fitCenter, centerInside, fitXY …) that decides how the bitmap is scaled inside the view box.
View showing a circular or horizontal progress indicator; set indeterminate=false and max plus progress for a determinate bar.
ViewGroup that holds exactly one child and scrolls it vertically; the child should use wrap_content height.
System service that turns a layout XML file into a view tree in code via inflate().
For a touch: dispatchTouchEvent → onTouchEvent → performClick → OnClickListener.onClick.

takeaways: An Android screen is a tree of View objects, and every View that has children is a ViewGroup whose job is measuring and placing them.
XML layouts and Java-built layouts produce the same tree; XML is only a declaration that LayoutInflater turns into objects.
Rotation destroys and recreates the activity, so any value the user typed must live in a ViewModel or be saved in onSaveInstanceState.
The action bar and its overflow list come from a menu XML file, and each click is routed back to your code by the item id.
A list view holds no data; the adapter builds row views on demand and recycles old rows to keep memory flat.
Each specialised view (ImageView, ProgressBar, ScrollView) has one measurement rule that decides whether it looks right.
A touch becomes a callback in one fixed order: dispatchTouchEvent, onTouchEvent, performClick, then your onClick.
Understanding this order explains why a clickable child can steal a touch from its parent.
Using dp for sizes, sp for text and a correct scaleType or layout_weight stops the same layout from breaking on a different phone.
bank_note: Long answers are expected to combine a small, correct XML or Java snippet with an explanation of which class does the measuring, saving or dispatching, so always name the callback and the class involved.

bank.q: Draw the view tree of a registration screen made of a title, two input fields, a submit button and an image, and explain how the tree is measured.
outline: Tree: LinearLayout root containing TextView, EditText, EditText, Button, ImageView
Measure pass walks the tree from root to leaves, then layout pass assigns positions
Parent passes width and height MeasureSpec to each child; child returns its desired size
A ViewGroup such as LinearLayout adds the children's heights for a vertical orientation
Explain onDraw happening after measure and layout

bank.q: Explain match_parent, wrap_content, dp, sp and layout_weight with one example each.
outline: match_parent: child asks for the whole parent size
wrap_content: child asks for exactly the content size
dp is density-independent; 1 dp = 1/160 inch, so the physical size stays the same on all screens
sp is dp scaled by the user's font setting, so use it for text only
layout_weight shares leftover space in a LinearLayout, weight 0 means fixed

bank.q: What is a configuration change? Describe step by step what Android does to an activity when the phone is rotated.
outline: Definition: rotation, keyboard, language, screen size, dark mode
onPause, onStop, onSaveInstanceState, onDestroy on the old instance
New instance created with matching configuration resources
onCreate, onStart, onResume; Bundle delivered to onCreate and onRestoreInstanceState
State in View objects with an id and saveEnabled is restored automatically

bank.q: How does an activity create an options menu from a menu XML file, and how does it know which item was clicked?
outline: Menu resource declared in res/menu with item id, title, showAsAction
onCreateOptionsMenu inflates with getMenuInflater().inflate()
Return true to show the menu
showAsAction=ifRoom or never decides action button versus overflow
onOptionsItemSelected receives the MenuItem; compare item.getItemId() with R.id values

bank.q: Why does a ListView never store its data? Explain the role of the adapter and of row recycling.
outline: ListView is a view; data lives in a list in your code
Adapter extends BaseAdapter: getCount, getView, getItem
getView is called only for visible rows plus a few
convertView is reused; you repopulate it instead of inflating again
ViewHolder keeps findViewById calls out of the scroll path

bank.q: Write the XML for a vertical LinearLayout holding a label, an EditText and a Button, where the EditText takes all leftover height and the button stays fixed.
outline: LinearLayout with android:orientation=vertical and match_parent width and height
android:padding on root and margins between children
EditText with layout_height=0dp and layout_weight=1
Button with layout_height=wrap_content and layout_weight omitted or 0
Text sizes in sp, dimensions in dp
State why 0dp plus weight is the correct idiom

bank.q: Write an activity that keeps a counter and a typed name correct across rotation, using onSaveInstanceState and onCreate.
outline: Declare the fields, initialise defaults or restore in onCreate(savedInstanceState)
Override onSaveInstanceState, put values in the Bundle with keys, call super
Restore with getString and getInt on the Bundle
Note that views with ids restore themselves; only your own fields need this
Mention the ViewModel alternative for larger state
Note the activity is destroyed so static or leaking references are wrong

bank.q: Write a menu XML file with two action items and one overflow item, and the Java code that inflates it and handles the clicks.
outline: res/menu/main.xml with three item tags, ids, titles, showAsAction values
onCreateOptionsMenu inflating and returning true
onOptionsItemSelected switching on getItemId()
Each case performs the action and returns true; default calls super
Explain that the action bar title is set separately

bank.q: Build a ListView of student names with a custom two-line row using an ArrayAdapter subclass and a ViewHolder.
outline: Row XML with two TextViews
Adapter extends ArrayAdapter, override getView
Inflate only when convertView is null, otherwise reuse
ViewHolder class holding the two TextView references, set as tag
Set name and roll number on the views, return convertView
Attach adapter to ListView with setAdapter, handle item click with AdapterView.OnItemClickListener

bank.q: Create a screen with one ImageView, one determinate ProgressBar and one Button entirely in Java, without any layout XML.
outline: Build a LinearLayout, set orientation and layout params
Create ImageView, setImageResource, set scaleType
Create ProgressBar with style horizontal, setMax, setProgress
Create Button, setOnClickListener, add views with addView and correct LayoutParams
Call setContentView(root)
Explain that this produces the same tree as XML

bank.q: Trace one finger tap on a Button from the moment the system delivers it to the activity, and explain why a parent can intercept the touch.
outline: Activity dispatches to the window, then to the root view
dispatchTouchEvent on the parent, then onInterceptTouchEvent decides pass down or take
Child's dispatchTouchEvent calls onTouchEvent if the child is clickable
onTouchEvent handles ACTION_DOWN, returns true to keep receiving the gesture
On ACTION_UP the view calls performClick, which calls the OnClickListener
Returning false on ACTION_DOWN means no further events arrive
Parents may intercept to support scrolling such as a ScrollView or a drawer

bank.q: A ScrollView shows nothing when its child has layout_height=match_parent, and an ImageView stretches faces out of shape with fitXY. Explain both and give the fix.
outline: ScrollView measures its single child with an unbounded height MeasureSpec
match_parent then resolves to a huge or zero value, so use wrap_content
ScrollView accepts only one direct child; wrap extra content in a LinearLayout
fitXY stretches the bitmap ignoring aspect ratio
centerCrop scales to fill and crops, fitCenter scales to fit inside, centerInside never enlarges
Choose scaleType by whether cropping or letterboxing is acceptable

bank.q: Compare android:configChanges with onSaveInstanceState for surviving rotation. Which should a beginner use, and when is the other justified?
outline: configChanges stops recreation and calls onConfigurationChanged
You must then re-do layout, reload alternate resources and re-measure by hand
onSaveInstanceState is the framework path, works with resource qualifiers and is testable
Saved state is limited to small Bundle data; use a ViewModel for heavy data
configChanges is justified for a media player or camera preview that must not restart
Recommend the save/restore path as default, configChanges as an exception with reasons

bank.q: Evaluate ListView against RecyclerView for a chat screen with ten thousand messages, and say what an adapter must do in each.
outline: ListView adapter: getView with convertView and ViewHolder pattern
RecyclerView separates recycling (LayoutManager) from binding (Adapter, ViewHolder)
RecyclerView supports item animations, horizontal lists and diffing with DiffUtil
ListView recycling still works, but binding and layout are fused
Both must avoid heavy work in the bind path; image loading should be off the main thread
Recommend RecyclerView with a stable id and DiffUtil for the chat case

glossary.def: A single screen with a user interface, managed by the Android framework through lifecycle callbacks.
The base class for any on-screen element that draws and can receive touch events.
A View that contains and positions other Views; all layouts are ViewGroups.
To read a layout or menu XML file and build the matching objects in memory.
A LinearLayout attribute that shares leftover space among children in proportion to the weight values.
A packed integer carrying a parent's size mode and size value that is passed to a child during measurement.
A size unit equal to 1/160 inch, so layouts keep the same physical size on every screen density.
A text size unit equal to one dp scaled by the user's chosen font size.
A key-value container that carries small saved state between activity instances.
The current set of device properties such as orientation, screen size, locale and density that Android matches to resource folders.
A folder suffix such as -land or -sw600dp that tells Android which version of a resource to load for the current configuration.
An XML file in res/menu describing menu items, their ids, titles and action-bar behaviour.
The list of menu items that did not fit as action buttons, opened from the three-dot icon.
An object that supplies row Views to a list-style view, one per data item, on demand.
A small holder object that caches child view references inside a recycled row so findViewById is not repeated.
A wheel-style input widget such as DatePicker, TimePicker or NumberPicker.
An ImageView property that decides whether the bitmap is stretched, cropped or letterboxed inside the view.
A progress indicator that spins without a known total, used when the duration cannot be computed.
Any graphic resource (bitmap, shape, selector) that a view can draw as its background or content.
The framework service, obtained by getLayoutInflater(), that converts layout XML into View objects.
An interface with one method, onClick(View), called when a clickable view completes a click.
The path by which a MotionEvent travels from the activity down the view tree to the view that consumes it.
The View method that fires the registered OnClickListener and plays the click sound.
The activity callback used to write UI state into a Bundle before the activity may be destroyed.
